title: Maitonphi: A Dramatic Adaptation
creator: Tangkhul Dramatic Troupe & TLS
author: Tangkhul Literature Society
notes: Stage play adaptation of the northern Tangkhul tragic love narrative, structured in five acts preserving traditional dialogue and song interludes.
indigenous_tangkhul_text: Act III: Maitonphi weaves the ceremonial Luirim cloth at her backstrap loom while singing an elegiac lament.
Shimreishang arrives at dusk, pledging undying devotion before departing on a perilous distant expedition.
The dramatic chorus echoes traditional folk song melodies (Pheichak Laa) commenting on fate's unyielding decree.
english_translation_text: Act III: Maitonphi weaves the ceremonial Luirim shawl at her backstrap loom, singing a haunting song of longing.
Shimreishang arrives at dusk, declaring his eternal devotion before departing on a perilous frontier journey.
The chorus chants antiphonal folk refrains, reflecting on the inexorable tragedy of human destiny.
literary_themes: Theatrical dramatization of the 17th-century Phungcham tragic romance
Integration of folk songs, weaving chants, and backstrap loom rhythms into stage performance
Tension between clan duties and individual emotional devotion
structure_and_meter: Five-act verse drama with alternating spoken dialogue, choral antiphony, and lyrical monologues.
critical_commentary: Adapted by the Tangkhul Dramatic Troupe and published by TLS in 1995, this play has been staged in community auditoriums across Ukhrul and Imphal to acclaim.

poetic_vocabulary_terms.Luirim-Tak: The rhythmic art of weaving the ceremonial shawl
poetic_vocabulary_terms.Kharashot-Laa: Elegiac song of enduring longing and sorrow
poetic_vocabulary_terms.Yarsho: Mountain path taken by travelers and warriors
poetic_vocabulary_terms.Ning-Khamathan: Pure and faithful devotion of the heart
